groups.name: Query semantics
groups.note: grains, transforms, joins, filters and composition

groups.name: Beyond query semantics
groups.note: results, tooling, security, serving and platform

rows.name: Coarser grain in the same query
rows.intent: Region totals on rows grouped by region and city.

slayer.caveat: partition_by=[] gives the grand total; takes lists, dotted join paths and time buckets.

malloy.caveat: Named dimensions must be output names. exclude() can reach outer levels of a nest:.

cube.how: SUM(rev) OVER (PARTITION BY region) over a nested SELECT ... MEASURE(revenue)
cube.caveat: Ad hoc only via the SQL API: SQL over the semantic result, without its guarantees. A model-declared grain measure does it in one query (not counted).

metricflow.text: No query-time partitioned aggregate; a metric filter joins only on the queried model's entities (verified).
metricflow.caveat: Mixed-grain metrics are an open request (#1998).

rows.comment: Malloy's all/exclude and SLayer's partition_by= are ad hoc; Cube Core ad hoc needs SQL over the results.

rows.name: Arithmetic across grains
rows.intent: Each city's share of its region, and of the grand total.

slayer.caveat: Grains union in one expression. A finer grain than the query works when aggregated back up; a bare finer-grain aggregate is rejected with PartitionKeyError.

malloy.caveat: Filtered forms: all(revenue { where: ... }). Finer grains need a pipeline stage.

cube.text: Window ratio over a nested semantic query in the SQL API
cube.caveat: Not counted: model-declared multi-stage measures.

metricflow.text: Ratio and derived metrics share one group-by, so share of parent isn't expressible.
metricflow.caveat: Open request #1998.

rows.comment: Same capability for share-of-parent.

rows.name: Re-aggregation
rows.intent: Per region, the unweighted average of city revenue totals.

malloy.how: orders -> { group_by: region, city; aggregate: revenue } -> { group_by: region; aggregate: avg(revenue) }
malloy.caveat: One stage fails with aggregate-of-aggregate.

cube.how: SELECT region, AVG(rev) FROM (SELECT region, city, MEASURE(revenue) rev ...) GROUP BY 1
cube.caveat: Verified. The docs warn that re-aggregating non-additive measures this way is wrong unless the inner grain matches.

metricflow.text: No aggregate of an aggregate, in a query or in a metric definition.
metricflow.caveat: Two-step aggregation is an open request (#653).

rows.comment: One expression in SLayer; a second stage or nested SQL query elsewhere.

rows.name: Transforms / time shift
rows.intent: "This measure one year earlier" while the date filter is the last 3 months; period-over-period change; running totals; lag.

slayer.caveat: Calendar-aware per group; the date range doesn't clip the lookback (probe-verified). lag/lead are row-based by design.

malloy.caveat: lag counts rows, and where: clips its input. Calendar shift = self-join on a query source.

cube.text: REST compareDateRange for fixed ranges side by side; SQL LAG() over a nested query
cube.caveat: Ad hoc shifts are row-based. Calendar-aware time_shift and rolling_window exist only as model declarations (not counted).

metricflow.text: No query-time shift or lag.
metricflow.caveat: Model-declared (not graded): an offset_window metric is calendar-aware and not clipped by start/end (verified).

rows.comment: Only SLayer shifts by calendar ad hoc; the others shift by rows or need a self-join.

rows.name: Calculated dimensions, filters, order
rows.intent: Group revenue by whether each customer's spend is high or low; filter and sort on computed values.

slayer.how: {"expression": "CASE WHEN sum(amount, partition_by=customer_id) > 100 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END", "name": "band"}

malloy.caveat: aggregate-in-dimension in one stage; order_by: takes output names only.

cube.text: Nested SQL: per-customer MEASURE(revenue) inside, CASE band and SUM outside; REST measure filters become HAVING
cube.caveat: The model-declared sub_query path hits a planner bug (#12020).

metricflow.caveat: Filters at an entity grain (verified). A band can't be a group-by; metric filters can't use metric_time (#1659); order only by selected items.

rows.comment: One inline dimension vs a derived source or nested SQL.

rows.name: Fields from many models, fan-out safe
rows.intent: Combine fields across joined models without multiplying rows.

slayer.caveat: Each aggregate computed at its own model; unproven to-one dimensions are associated with a warning.

malloy.caveat: Symmetric aggregates. Bug (#1762): a join_many leaf count counts a childless parent as 1.

cube.text: Declared joins with relationship: many_to_one
cube.caveat: Verified: primary-key dedup and one CTE per cube, even for raw SUM measures.

metricflow.text: Entity-based joins, many-to-one and one-to-one only; fan-out paths are never offered (verified).
metricflow.caveat: Up to two hops. One dimension gets different names from different facts (region__name vs customer__region__name).

rows.comment: Four sound designs; the differences are in defaults and in who picks the aggregation point. MetricFlow refuses fan-out paths outright.

rows.name: Deep composition
rows.intent: A mixed-grain expression, then a time shift, then a re-aggregation, all in one expression.

slayer.caveat: Uncompilable shapes fail with a typed error before the database (probe-verified).

malloy.caveat: sum(row_number()) reaches the database (#3105).

cube.text: Stacked nested SQL queries
cube.caveat: Each layer is hand-written SQL over the semantic result, without its guarantees.

metricflow.text: Each composition layer is a model-declared metric.

rows.comment: The biggest design difference. Stages and named measures are easier to inspect individually.

rows.name: Population inference
rows.intent: Omit the root model; measures never change which rows come back.

slayer.text: Inferred from dimensions and plain filters only; ties fail with PopulationInferenceError.

malloy.text: A source is always named; its rows are the result's rows.

cube.text: Queries never name a root; Cube picks it from the join graph
cube.caveat: The default planner usually roots at the dimension's cube (verified). Pin with the joinHints query option.

metricflow.text: Each metric is rooted at its own model; multi-metric queries full-outer-join the per-metric results (verified).
metricflow.caveat: Revenue by region is rooted at orders: no row for a region without orders.

rows.comment: Cube also infers, but heuristically; SLayer's rule is fixed and fails closed on ties.

rows.name: No silently wrong numbers
rows.intent: Fail loudly with a reason, or warn about what was approximated.

slayer.caveat: Typed errors and structured warnings; every SLayer probe returns the right numbers or fails with a typed error (verified).

malloy.text: Uncomputable join_many aggregates are rejected; an ambiguous join_one sum/avg warns bad-join-usage.
malloy.caveat: Verified gaps: #1762, #3105; docs state the rule backwards (docs #346).

cube.text: Strong fan-out dedup; joins without primary keys fail to compile. No warnings channel.
cube.caveat: Verified silent cases: an ignored order-by (Q13, #282), re-truncation accepted (Q18), a second fact grouped by another cube's time dimension (C19); SQL post-processing can be wrong past 50,000 rows (documented).

metricflow.text: Fan-out is prevented structurally: MetricFlow refuses rather than multiplies.
metricflow.caveat: Verified: NULL (not 0) counts for childless parents, and the period_agg and raw-where bugs below.

rows.comment: SLayer has the most explicit machinery (modes, typed errors, warnings) and no open silent case in its probes; Cube and MetricFlow prevent fan-out by construction.

rows.name: Filters across one-to-many joins
rows.intent: Customers with at least one OK order, counted once, including under OR / NOT.

slayer.caveat: Pushed down as EXISTS; each customer once. orders.id is null = "no orders".

malloy.caveat: Each customer once. No exists; the count() = 0 anti-join is broken by #1762.

cube.text: Verified: customers.count filtered on orders.status counts each customer once; OR across cubes works row by row
cube.caveat: "Has no orders" (notSet) works only when customers is the chosen root.

metricflow.text: To-many filters via {{ Metric(...) }} at an entity: at least one order counted once, OR across models, "has no orders" via IS NULL (verified).
metricflow.caveat: Dimension('order__status') in a customers query is refused; "at least one OK order" needs a filtered metric in the model.

rows.comment: For a plain condition, SLayer, Malloy and Cube agree. NOT is "has none" in none of them; Malloy and Cube count a customer with no orders as matching a negated condition, SLayer (SQL NULL logic) doesn't.

rows.name: Rolling time windows
rows.intent: Trailing 90 days of any aggregate, including count distinct.

slayer.caveat: Time-based, every aggregation; date bounds don't clip the lookback; composes with arithmetic and transforms.

malloy.caveat: Row frames only; no rolling count distinct.

cube.text: SQL window frames over a daily nested query
cube.caveat: Row frames only ad hoc; no rolling count distinct. Time-based rolling_window is a model declaration (not counted).

metricflow.text: No query-time windows.
metricflow.caveat: Model-declared window: 90 days is exact by day, incl. count distinct; at month grain it hits the period_agg bug.

rows.comment: Only SLayer has time-based windows ad hoc; the others count rows.

rows.name: Aggregates as arguments
rows.intent: Aggregate an expression spanning models; weight by a coarser-grain aggregate.

malloy.caveat: No aggregate inside an aggregate.

cube.text: Pushdown expressions over cube members; a weight from a nested aggregate in SQL
cube.caveat: Cross-cube expression measures exist only in the model (not counted).

metricflow.text: A measure's expr sees only its own model's columns; no aggregate as a weight.

rows.comment: The cross-model expression works everywhere; the aggregate-as-parameter is ad hoc only in SLayer.

rows.name: Order by what you don't show
rows.intent: Top 10 statuses by revenue, displaying only the count.

cube.text: Verified: ordering by an unselected measure works
cube.caveat: Silently ignored: an unselected dimension in order is left out of the SQL without an error (see #282).

metricflow.text: Order only by selected metrics and group-by items (verified).

rows.comment: A common top-N pattern.

rows.name: Ranking and streaks
rows.intent: Filter on rank in the same query; "3+ consecutive positive months".

slayer.caveat: Streaks count calendar periods, so an empty month breaks them (verified).

malloy.caveat: Rank filters need a second stage; streaks 2+.

cube.how: RANK() OVER (...) in an outer SQL query, filtered one level up
cube.caveat: Verified; needed a CAST around the rank. Streaks by hand in SQL.

metricflow.text: Global order plus limit only.

rows.comment: For top-N per group, Malloy's nest: is a fair match.

rows.name: Multi-stage queries
rows.intent: A query feeding another; save a query as a reusable model; re-bucket dates downstream.

slayer.text: Named stages form a dependency graph; save as a query-backed model; re-bucket at equal or coarser grain.

malloy.caveat: Each -> a CTE; views refine with +.

cube.text: An outer SQL query over an inner semantic query (verified)
cube.caveat: Saving a result as a model means changing the model.

metricflow.text: Saved queries can't be used as sources.
metricflow.caveat: Exports need the dbt platform.

rows.comment: Malloy's is the richest.

rows.name: Inline model extension
rows.intent: Add a column, measure or join for one query without editing the model.

cube.text: SQL API pushdown expressions over dimensions and aggregations (verified)
cube.caveat: No ad-hoc members over REST; no ad-hoc joins.

metricflow.text: No expressions in group-by; raw SQL only inside a where, around a Jinja reference (verified).

rows.comment: Cube's model-first design shows here.

rows.name: Saved measures that compose
rows.intent: Reuse a named formula in transforms and arithmetic; save transforms as measures.

malloy.caveat: A window expression can't be saved as a measure.

cube.text: Existing measures combine in SQL arithmetic (MEASURE(a) / MEASURE(b))
cube.caveat: Saving a period-over-period formula needs a model change.

metricflow.text: Queries use named metrics.
metricflow.caveat: Ratio, derived and offset composition must be declared in the model.

rows.comment: Only SLayer saves a transform as a reusable measure without writing model code.

rows.name: Time-bucket safety
rows.intent: Refuse a day breakdown of a column already truncated to month.

slayer.text: Typed error; Column.granularity set on query-backed models (probe-verified).

malloy.text: m.day returns month starts labelled as days.

cube.text: Verified: a day query on a month-truncated dimension returns first-of-month "days"

metricflow.text: A month-grain dimension refuses a day or week breakdown and a day-grain filter (verified).

rows.comment: SLayer and MetricFlow refuse; the others return mislabelled rows.

rows.name: Agent & API surface
rows.intent: How an agent actually issues queries.

slayer.text: MCP, REST, CLI and Python.
slayer.caveat: Queries are schema-validated JSON.

malloy.text: Publisher MCP and REST; loadRestrictedQuery() sandboxes LLM-written queries.

cube.text: REST (JSON), GraphQL and a Postgres-wire SQL API

metricflow.caveat: No network API in open source; it's a dbt platform feature.

rows.comment: JSON (SLayer, Cube), a text language (Malloy), or CLI and Python arguments (MetricFlow). MCP servers are C24.

rows.name: Relative & typed filters
rows.intent: "Last 3 days", "this quarter", value lists and ranges without hand-computing bounds.

slayer.caveat: Relative tokens, periods (day to year, ISO week) and open-ended ranges, verified with a pinned clock; a period bound covers the whole period.

cube.caveat: Verified, incl. "from 500 days ago to now"; typed operators like inDateRange, notSet.

metricflow.text: Absolute start/end, widened to the query grain (verified).
metricflow.caveat: Relative ranges need raw SQL date math in a where.

rows.comment: All but MetricFlow take relative ranges in the query.

rows.name: Calendar expressions
rows.intent: Day-of-week, date differences, date arithmetic and time zones as portable expressions.

slayer.caveat: Portable across engines (verified). No time zones.

cube.text: Query timezone; EXTRACT(DOW ...) in the SQL API over a nested query (verified)
cube.caveat: No day-of-week granularity; date math in raw SQL. timezone moves DATE values back a day in negative-offset zones (#10166).

metricflow.caveat: Verified. Date math only as raw SQL in filters; time zones not documented.

rows.comment: Malloy's portable date algebra is richest.

rows.name: Nested source data
rows.intent: Query arrays and repeated records with fan-out-safe aggregation.

slayer.caveat: List columns aggregate fan-out-safe beside parent aggregates (Q27); struct columns are opaque.

cube.text: No nested types in queries
cube.caveat: Arrays must be unnested in the model.

metricflow.text: Not documented.

rows.comment: A headline Malloy feature.

rows.name: Saved queries & refinement
rows.intent: Reuse a saved query and extend the query itself with dimensions, measures or filters, not only post-process its output.

slayer.caveat: Dimensions, measures, filters, order and limit merge into the saved query's final stage; a conflicting redefinition is a typed error (verified).

cube.text: No saved query shapes in Core
cube.caveat: Views curate members; they aren't query shapes.

metricflow.text: A saved query takes an extra where, order and limit (verified).
metricflow.caveat: Not extra metrics or group-bys.

rows.comment: Malloy and SLayer merge any clause into a saved query; MetricFlow's saved queries take a few extra clauses.

rows.name: Nested / hierarchical results
rows.intent: Per region, a sub-table of top customers, in one result.

slayer.text: One nest flattens: partition_by for the region total, rank for the top N, ties included (verified).
slayer.caveat: Sibling nests need one query each.

malloy.how: nest: by_customer is { ...; limit: 5 }; sibling nests in one query (verified)

cube.text: Flat results, GraphQL included.

metricflow.text: Flat results.

rows.comment: Malloy's flagship feature.

rows.name: Explicit aggregate locality
rows.intent: From orders, average a customer field per customer vs per order.

slayer.text: The reading follows where the inputs live (all verified): avg(customers.credit) is per customer, even as a measure declared on orders; an orders filter keeps customers with orders; an orders-side column (credit: customers.credit, in a model extension) reads per order.

malloy.caveat: The per-customer form covers only customers reached through orders.

cube.text: Measures aggregate at their own cube by default (per entity)
cube.caveat: A per-order reading of a customer field needs SQL over joined members or a model change.

metricflow.text: A measure lives in its own model, so an average of a customer field is per customer by construction.
metricflow.caveat: A per-order weighting needs a joining dbt model.

rows.comment: From orders, SLayer's plain cross-model average includes customers with no orders; Malloy's includes only those reached through the join.

rows.name: Metrics without a join path
rows.intent: Events per customer in one query, though no join path links events to customers.

slayer.caveat: Computed over events' own rows and repeated on every row with an unrelated_dataset warning; a spine time dimension buckets it per period, warning-free when it is the only dimension; grouping by an events column is a typed error (verified).

malloy.caveat: Symmetric aggregates keep totals exact (verified), but you write the join, a time bucket needs a hand-written on, and nothing stops a row-multiplying group-by.

cube.text: Unrelated grand totals side by side; any dimension, or the SQL API, fails with Can't find join path (verified).
cube.caveat: The legacy planner refuses even the totals. A model-declared 1 = 1 join gives the total on every customer row (not counted).

metricflow.text: Metrics from unrelated models combine when grouped by metric_time or by nothing (verified).
metricflow.caveat: Grouping by a customer is refused, and an empty month reads NULL, not 0; a cross-model ratio is a model-declared derived metric (not counted).

rows.comment: Only SLayer combines unrelated models under the population's own dimensions without a written join; Cube and MetricFlow stop at totals (MetricFlow also at metric_time), and Malloy's join_cross is a capable workaround.

rows.name: List columns
rows.intent: Customers tagged vip, tagged both vip and eu, counted per tag, and each region's tag set, over a tags VARCHAR[] column.

slayer.caveat: A repeated tag counts its customer once per tag under associate, element aggregates sit next to customer aggregates without fan-out, and NULL elements are ignored (verified).

malloy.caveat: Symmetric aggregates keep customer counts exact (verified); both tags need a having: per tag, and a tag set is a nest:, not a list value.

cube.text: A list dimension groups by whole lists, its contains filter is a database error, and the SQL API has no list functions (verified).
cube.caveat: A model-declared one-row-per-tag cube with a synthetic key counts customers per tag; next to a customer count either planner's root selection drops customers (not counted).

metricflow.text: A raw-SQL where (list_contains(...), list_has_all(...)) filters by tags (verified).
metricflow.caveat: Grouping by the list dimension groups by whole lists; per-tag counts need a one-row-per-tag dbt model (not counted).

rows.comment: SLayer and Malloy treat a list column as rows of its elements without double counting; Cube and MetricFlow see whole lists, MetricFlow filtering them only through raw SQL.

rows.name: Rendering & tooling
rows.intent: Charts, dashboards, notebooks, drill-down, delivery.

slayer.text: Headless; returns data.

malloy.text: Rendering tags, notebooks, VS Code, Explorer.

cube.text: Playground only.
cube.caveat: Workbooks and dashboards are Cloud features.

metricflow.text: CLI tables, CSV and a plan SVG; no charts.

rows.comment: A product-focus difference.

rows.name: Pre-aggregation & materialization
rows.intent: Rollup tables chosen automatically; caching and refresh.

slayer.text: An opt-in in-memory result cache only.

cube.text: Rollups, refresh keys, partitions, Cube Store

metricflow.text: Not in open source.

rows.comment: Cube's defining feature.

rows.name: Parameters & row-level security
rows.intent: Runtime parameters; scope every query of a session to one tenant.

slayer.text: Engine policy the agent can't override; unlisted tables fail closed (probe-verified). {var} parameters.

cube.text: Access policies with row_level; security context; per-tenant data sources
cube.caveat: userAttributes is Cloud-only; Core uses the security context.

metricflow.text: No parameters or row-level security in open source.

rows.comment: Matters most for agent and embedded deployments.

rows.name: Database coverage
rows.intent: Where it runs.

slayer.text: 8 engines tested live, 4 more by SQL generation.

cube.text: 26 sources, incl. streaming (ksqlDB, Materialize) and MongoDB.

metricflow.text: Nine SQL renderers: BigQuery, DuckDB, Redshift, Postgres, Snowflake, Databricks, Trino, Vertica, Athena.

rows.comment: Cube's list is the longest.

rows.name: Model authoring & reuse
rows.intent: How models get written, shared and kept in sync.

slayer.text: YAML/JSON; dbt, Cube and OSI importers.

cube.text: YAML/JS with Jinja/Python generation, extends, cube_dbt

metricflow.text: dbt YAML semantic models next to the dbt models they read.

rows.comment: Models as data (SLayer), as code (Malloy), generated (Cube), or beside the dbt models they read (MetricFlow).

rows.name: Value index
rows.intent: Find which field holds "SANTA CRUZ", for filter suggestions and LLM grounding.

slayer.text: Sampled top values per column feed search.

cube.text: No documented value index in Core.

metricflow.how: mf list dimension-values queries live values; no index.

rows.comment: Relevant to agent accuracy on filter values.

rows.name: Authoring feedback loop
rows.intent: Catch bad references and types before running.

slayer.text: Save-time validation, dry_run, typed errors; no IDE support.

cube.text: Compile errors on reload (verified)
cube.caveat: No language-server support documented.

metricflow.how: dbt parse, mf validate-configs (checks the warehouse too) and --explain (verified).

rows.comment: SLayer has no editor tooling.

rows.name: SQL interop
rows.intent: Native SQL anywhere, and semantic queries inside SQL.

slayer.text: SQL models and columns; a Postgres-wire facade accepting a SQL subset.
slayer.caveat: No full SQL over semantic queries.

cube.text: SQL API with MEASURE(), pushdown and post-processing (verified)

metricflow.text: Raw SQL in expressions and filters.
metricflow.caveat: Semantic queries inside SQL need the dbt platform (JDBC).

rows.comment: Malloy and Cube go both ways.

rows.name: Portable expression library
rows.intent: The same function means the same thing on every engine.

slayer.text: One library (strings, math, regex, JSON, dates, TEXT-vs-number coercion) with one meaning on every engine, verified per engine.
slayer.caveat: Postgres 16+ for NULL-on-error JSON reads and TRY_CAST; SQL Server 2025+ for regex.

malloy.text: Broad standard library plus a native escape.

cube.text: Model SQL is warehouse-specific; only SQL API functions are transpiled.

metricflow.text: MetricFlow renders its own time, window and offset constructs per dialect.
metricflow.caveat: User expressions are raw SQL.

rows.comment: Overlaps with Q21.

rows.name: BI connectivity
rows.intent: Tableau, Metabase, Excel or Power BI query the semantic layer directly.

slayer.text: Postgres-wire SQL API and Arrow Flight SQL.
slayer.caveat: Read-only, a SQL subset; no MDX/DAX.

malloy.text: REST, React SDK and MCP only.

cube.text: Postgres-wire SQL API (verified)
cube.caveat: MDX and DAX APIs are Enterprise-only.

metricflow.text: A dbt platform feature.

rows.comment: Both speak the Postgres wire protocol; SLayer adds Arrow Flight SQL.

rows.name: Curated semantic surfaces
rows.intent: Expose a vetted subset of members with pinned join paths.

slayer.text: Facade models over named join edges; hidden keeps the models behind them out of listings (verified).

cube.text: Views with join_path, includes, folders

metricflow.text: Saved queries.

rows.comment: Also Cube's answer to join-path ambiguity (Q8).

rows.name: Member-level security & masking
rows.intent: Hide or mask specific fields per user.

slayer.text: Row-level only.

metricflow.text: Not in open source.

rows.comment: Enterprise-governance territory.

rows.name: Embeddable UI components
rows.intent: Ready-made UI components (charts, tables, query builders) that render the layer's results in your own app.

slayer.text: Headless: APIs only, no UI components.

malloy.text: Results render with @malloydata/render; Publisher embed / React SDK; token check unfinished per its docs.

cube.text: Headless React bindings (QueryRenderer, QueryBuilder) over REST; no charts or tables
cube.caveat: iframe embedding with sessions is a Cloud feature.

metricflow.text: Not in open source.

rows.comment: Malloy renders results with its own components; Cube Core ships headless React bindings; hosted embedding is a Cloud feature.

rows.name: Custom calendars & granularities
rows.intent: Fiscal years, retail 4-5-4, 15-minute buckets.

slayer.caveat: Datasource granularities work as time dimensions, time_shift units and spine buckets: fiscal years and 15-minute buckets verified. No retail 4-5-4 calendars.

metricflow.text: Custom granularities from the time spine, e.g. an April fiscal year (verified).

rows.comment: Interval-based grains in SLayer and Cube; MetricFlow's spine columns can hold any calendar.

rows.name: Drill-across fact tables
rows.intent: Combine unrelated facts (orders, returns) over shared dimensions.

cube.text: Multi-fact queries and views, one CTE per fact (verified)

metricflow.text: Metrics from two fact models on one axis (verified).
metricflow.caveat: Refused when the dimension's entity path differs per fact.

rows.comment: Fan-out safety makes this work in all four.

rows.name: Cross-database queries
rows.intent: Join models living in different databases.

slayer.caveat: Verified live against Postgres and MySQL catalogs. Models on two SLayer datasources still can't meet in one query.

malloy.caveat: Documented. Sources on two Malloy connections can't be joined; a DuckDB connection can also ATTACH other databases.

cube.text: Trino driver; cubes whose sql_table names different catalogs join as usual
cube.caveat: From source, not verified here; catalog-qualified sql_table isn't documented. Cubes on two Cube data sources need a rollup_join (Preview) in Cube Store.

metricflow.text: dbt-trino: models in different catalogs via database:, joined through entities
metricflow.caveat: From source, not verified here. One adapter per dbt project, so no federation beyond Trino.

rows.comment: All four reach several databases through Trino catalogs; natively, only Cube (rollup_join, Preview) and Malloy (a DuckDB connection with ATTACH) come close.

rows.name: Drill-down to records
rows.intent: From an aggregate, fetch the underlying rows.

slayer.text: Raw-rows query mode; no declared drill members.

metricflow.text: Dimension-only queries list rows of declared dimensions (verified).

rows.comment: Mostly a UI concern.

rows.name: Entity-graph join inference
rows.intent: Joins found automatically from declared keys, including multi-hop.

slayer.text: Join edges traversed both ways, with dotted multi-hop paths inferred.

malloy.text: Joins declared per source; dotted paths follow them.

cube.text: Path-finding over the join graph, plus joinHints.

metricflow.text: An entity graph, up to two hops.

rows.comment: Similar power; the differences are direction and hop limits.

rows.name: Shared time axis across facts
rows.intent: One time dimension for metrics from different fact tables.

slayer.caveat: A built-in spine each model joins through its own date column; per group too; two equally short routes fail loudly (verified).

malloy.text: A hand-made calendar source joined to each fact; symmetric aggregates keep it exact (verified).

cube.text: Needs a model-declared dates cube.
cube.caveat: Query-only, a second fact lands in the months of the time dimension's own cube: returns counted in their customers' order months (verified).

metricflow.caveat: Months with either fact; empty months only with a model change (verified).

rows.comment: SLayer and MetricFlow give every fact one time axis; elsewhere it is a hand-made calendar.

rows.name: Gap filling / time spine
rows.intent: Rows for empty periods, zero-filled.

slayer.caveat: Every bucket in range, per group too; change, cumsum, lag, streaks and windows see the empty months (verified). A lower bound is required.

cube.text: Client-side fillMissingDates only.

metricflow.caveat: Declared on the metric; a query's start/end alone doesn't fill (verified).

rows.comment: SLayer fills in any query; MetricFlow per declared metric.

rows.name: Semi-additive measures
rows.intent: Balances: sum across accounts, last value over time.

slayer.caveat: One expression per query: the latest balance per account, then summed.

cube.text: No recipe.

rows.comment: Declared once in MetricFlow; one query expression in SLayer; a pipeline elsewhere.

rows.name: Point-in-time (SCD Type II) joins
rows.intent: Join a fact to the dimension row valid at that time.

slayer.text: A custom SQL join.

cube.text: Custom SQL.

rows.comment: A MetricFlow specialty.

rows.name: Open interchange spec
rows.intent: Import and export semantic definitions in a shared format.

slayer.text: Imports OSI, dbt and Cube; no export.

cube.text: None.

metricflow.text: Writes an Open Semantic Interchange document (verified); cumulative and conversion metrics can't be represented.

rows.comment: OSI has been renamed Apache Ossie.

rows.name: Built-in MCP server
rows.intent: An agent connects a database, explores it, edits models and queries over MCP, with nothing extra to deploy.

slayer.caveat: Datasource, ingestion, model-editing, query, search and memory tools, plus built-in help; from an empty store to an answer over MCP alone (probe-verified).

malloy.text: Publisher MCP: get_context, execute_query, compile_model, reload_package, docs search; skills as prompts.
malloy.caveat: No tool writes models: the agent edits .malloy files on disk, then reloads.

cube.text: No MCP server in Core.
cube.caveat: Cube's MCP server is hosted by Cube Cloud (cubecloud.dev/mcp).

metricflow.text: No MCP server; the open-source dbt-mcp's semantic-layer tools call the dbt platform API.
metricflow.caveat: Without a platform account, dbt-mcp offers only CLI, codegen and LSP tools.

rows.comment: SLayer and Malloy ship one; SLayer's can also create and change models.

rows.name: Agent memories
rows.intent: An agent saves what it learned about the data; later agents get it back when they touch the same columns.

slayer.caveat: A note, or a vetted example query, tied to models and columns; search and inspect return it with them (probe-verified).

malloy.text: No memory store; a Publisher skill tells agents to write learnings as #(doc) annotations into model files.

cube.text: No agent memory in Core.
cube.caveat: Cube Cloud's AI agent has memories, rules and certified queries.

metricflow.text: Hand-written description and meta in YAML only.

rows.comment: Only SLayer keeps notes that agents write and read back.

rows.name: Smart retrieval
rows.intent: Find the models, fields and notes a question needs without loading the whole schema.

slayer.how: search(question="which city does a customer live in")
slayer.caveat: One ranked list of models, columns, measures and memories: stemmed full text, entity overlap, optional embeddings, plus a graph filter (probe-verified without embeddings).

malloy.caveat: Ranks sources, fields, joins and views of one package per call; BM25, embeddings with an API key.

cube.text: Core has only /v1/meta, the full metadata, with no search.
cube.caveat: Search over the data model is a Cube Cloud feature.

metricflow.text: mf list metrics --search matches metric names by substring.
metricflow.caveat: dbt-mcp's search tools need the dbt platform.

rows.comment: SLayer and Malloy rank schema context for agents; SLayer ranks memories in the same list.

rows.name: Auto-ingestion
rows.intent: Point it at a database and get queryable models, with joins from foreign keys.

slayer.caveat: Foreign keys become joins and comments descriptions; join cardinality from the keys. Re-runs add without overwriting (probe-verified).

malloy.text: conn.table('x') reads a table's columns at compile time; joins and measures are written by hand.

cube.caveat: A one-time scaffold that rewrites the model folder. Foreign keys are read only on Postgres, MySQL and Redshift; elsewhere joins come from *_id names (source).

metricflow.text: Semantic models are hand-written YAML; dbt-codegen scaffolds sources and staging models only.

rows.comment: SLayer and Cube generate models with joins; only SLayer re-ingests additively.

rows.name: Runtime model editing
rows.intent: Add a column, measure or join through an API and use it in the next query: no build, no restart.

slayer.caveat: Over MCP, REST, CLI or Python; the next query sees it (probe-verified).

malloy.text: Edit .malloy files, then reload_package or watch mode; no restart.
malloy.caveat: No API writes model files.

cube.text: Dev mode re-reads changed model files on the next request; repositoryFactory + schemaVersion load models from elsewhere.
cube.caveat: No API writes models in Core; API editing is a Cube Cloud feature.

metricflow.text: Edit YAML, then dbt parse rebuilds the manifest mf reads.
metricflow.caveat: No create or edit API.

rows.comment: Only SLayer takes model changes through its own API.

rows.name: Schema drift handling
rows.intent: Notice when the warehouse changes under the models, and say what to fix.

slayer.caveat: A failing query names the drifted model; validate_models returns the edit_model call that fixes it; re-ingestion keeps hand edits (probe-verified).

malloy.text: A dropped column is a compile error with file and line at reload; Publisher keeps serving the previous model, flagged stale.
malloy.caveat: Nothing checks the warehouse until a reload or compile.

cube.text: Nothing checks models against the warehouse; a dropped column is a raw database error at query time.
cube.caveat: cubejs validate compiles the files without a database connection.

metricflow.caveat: Dry-runs each element against the warehouse and names the broken one; column types aren't compared, and queries surface the raw warehouse error.

rows.comment: SLayer detects drift at query time too and proposes the fix; elsewhere it is a validation run or a compile error.
